RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the February 26, 2002/Phalguna 7, 1923 ( Saka)
————
(Ministries:  Civil Aviation; Commerce and Industry; Finance;  Petroleum
and Natural Gas; Tourism and Culture; Water Resources)
Total number of questions—20

Contract engineers in EIL
*1. SHRI GOPALSINH G. SOLANKI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to refer to
answer to Unstarred Question 1802 given
in the Rajya Sabha on the 7th August,
2001, and state:
(a) whether 50 per cent of vacancies/
requirements of management trainees will
be filled on an annual basis from contract
engineers as decided by the Board of
Engineers India Limited (EIL);
(b) if so, the number of contract
engineers who have been recruited/
absorbed by the management of EIL as
on 31st January, 2002 and if not, the
reasons for delay in re-instating these
contract engineers; and
(c) whether Government would absorb
all the contract engineers within a time-
bound programme and if not, the reasons
therefor?
Deposits with commercial banks
*2. SHRI C.O. POULOSE: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been a sharp
decline in deposits  with the scheduled
commercial banks;
(b) whether the fall in deposits is direct
impact of recent decision to cut down the
interest rates on deposits; and
(c) if so, whether Government would
reconsider the interest structure in these
banks in order to attract more deposits?
VRS for Associate Banks of SBI
*3. DR. Y. LAKSHMI PRASAD: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that various
employees of the associate banks of the
State Bank of India who have submitted
their applications for VRS on 31st March,
2001, have not been considered as
10 per cent of the staff strength despite
clear instructions issued by Government
in this regard;
(b) if so, the details of such employees
whose applications have not been
considered by the banks, bank-wise and
region-wise;
(c) by when the remaining applications
are likely to be considered in view of the
instructions; and
(d) by when V RS policy is likely to be
opened again for the employees?

Scam in Krushi Urban Co-operative
Bank in Andhra Pradesh
*4. SHRI K.M. SAIFULLAH:
DR. Y. LAKSHMI  PRASAD:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a fresh scam
of over compensation of some depositors
in Krushi Urban Co-operative Bank in
Andhra Pradesh has come to light;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken against the erring
officials for their involvement in the
scam?
Revision of freight charges by IBP
†*5. SHRI MUNAVVAR HASAN:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that IBP
company had taken a decision to increase
freight charges for the transporters of
Delhi in its meeting held on
29th November, 2001;
(b) if so, since when the said increase
came into effect;
(c) the names and addresses of the
transporters whose freight has been
increased and the outstanding amount paid
to each of them;
(d) the names and addresses of the
transporters whose outstanding amounts
have not yet been paid with details of
outstanding amount of each of such
transporters; and
(e) by when all transporters will be
paid their dues?
Recapitalisation of co-operative banks
*6. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the National Bank for
Agricultural and Rural Development
(NABARD) has demanded Rs. 6000
crores for recap italisation of co-operative
Banks to ensure adequate credit flow; and
(b) if so, what is Government's reaction
thereto?
Economic growth
*7. SHRI  SOLIPETA RAMA-
CHANDRA  REDDY:
SHRI  RUMANDLA
RAMACHANDRAIAH:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention
has been drawn to the news-item
captioned "Economy grew by just 4 per
cent last year" which appeared in The
Times of India dated the 1st February,
2002;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government
declared 5.2 per cent growth of economy
during 2000-01 and 6.4 per cent during
1999-2000;
(d) if so, in what manner it has now
been declared only 4 per cent growth and
how far agricultural and other products
were affected during the period; and
(e) the steps being taken by
Government to improve the economy?
Anti-dumping cases
*8. SHR I KRISHNA KUMAR
BIRLA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to sta te:
(a) whether Government have initiated
anti-dumping cases against several foreign
companies during 2001;

Target for export
†*9. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH
'LALAN':
SHRI  RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that export in
the first nine months of the current year
has not been made as per the target fixed;
(b) if so, the annual target fixed
alongwith the export made so far; and
(c) the name of those ten items
exported maximum from the country?
India’s share in world exports
*10. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that although
exports during 2000-2001 rose by 18 per
cent to touch $ 44 billion, yet they were
lower than other Asian countries like
Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor,
indicating India’s present share of world’s
exports;
(c) whether under new medium-term
export strategy, Government would be
able to achieve the target of annual exports
of $ 80 billion by 2007 as well as
cornering India’s share of world exports
to 1 per cent; and
(d) whether tax rebates, export
subsidies given by Government would
stay or India's strategy would be WTO
compatible?
Security arrangements at IGIA
*11. SHRI ABANI ROY:
SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the BCAS + at IGI A@ has
recently conducted a security audit and
recommended steps to prevent serious
breach of security;
(b) if so, Government's reaction on
such recommendations;
(c) whether the security arrangements
around IGIA are inadequate to face any
terrorists threat; and
(d) if so, the plans formulated to
strengthen the security arrangements
around IGIA in the Capital?
Minimum Support Price for coffee
*12. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
introduce Minimum Support Price (MSP)
for coffee;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when the practice of declaring
MSP for coffe e is likely to start?

Instalment of Dearness Allowance
*13. SHRI RAJU PARMAR:
SHRI BHAGATRAM
MANHAR:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the next
instalment of Dearness Allowance/
Dearness Relief to the Central
Government Employees/Pensioners has
become due w.e.f. 1st January, 2002;
(b) if so, the details of increase to be
given to the Central Government
Employees/Pensioners; and
(c) by when Government will take a
final decision in this regard?
MoU over Brahmaputra River
*14. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)
has recently been signed between China
and India with regard to the Brahmaputra
River;
(b) if so, the details and the objectives
thereof;  and
(c) what follow-up steps Government
propose to take to plan and prepare for
the floods and also work out water
resources development plans in the
catchment areas as a result of the proposed
agreement?
Burden on income tax payers
*15. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
only 2 per cent of the country's population
is income tax assessee who pay income
tax for the 98 per cent of non-tax paying
population;
(b) if so, whether more burden by
imposing 2 per cent surcharge on the
existing income tax payers is justified;
(c) if not, whether this will encourage
people to shy away from becoming honest
tax payers; and
(d) if so, the action taken by
Government in this regard?
World Heritage Sites
*16. SHRI RAJNATH SINGH
'SURYA': Will the Minister of TOURISM
AND CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have failed to get any of its sites declared
as World Heritage Site this year also;
(b) if so, whether it was due to delay
in submitting the request to UNESCO;
(c) if so, whether any responsibility for
this lapse has been fixed;
(d) if so, the action proposed against
those guilty; and
(e) if not, by when it would be done?
Allotment of LPG dealership in H.P.
†*17. SHRI  ANIL  SHARMA: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
allotment of LPG dealership is done
arbitrarily by the Oil and Gas Board in
the rural/urban areas of Himachal
Pradesh;
(b) whether it is also a fact that in the
process of allotment of such dealership,
SC unemployed graduate ladies and

(c) in what manner oil/gas is made

Expansion of Oil Refineries
*18. SHRI ANANTA SETHI: Will the
Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether steps have been taken
during the Ninth Five Year Plan to increase
the capacity of refineries;
(b) if so, the details of the expansion
programmes carried out in that Plan
period;
(c) whether production has increased
after expansion; and
(d) if so, the refinery-wise details
thereof alongwith the projections made for
the Tenth Five Year Plan?
Irrigation projects in Karnataka
*19. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN: Will
the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large
number of irrigation projects pertaining
to Karnataka are pending for approval;
(b) whether it is also a fact that these
projects were discussed with the State
Government in the recent meeting in
Bangalore; and
(c) if so, by when these projects are
likely to be cleared?
Schemes for enhancing water in
Himachal Pradesh
†*20. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of Centrally sponsored
schemes being implemented to assist
Himachal Pradesh for enhancing water
resources and its exploitation;
(b) the year-wise amount allocated to
Himachal Pradesh during the last three
years alongwith the amount released,
year-wise; and
(c) the State's achievement with regard
to preservation of additional water and
exploitation of water resources?
